title: CM Yuva Udyami Yojana UP: Rs 5 Lakh Loan, Apply Online
meta_description: CM Yuva Udyami Yojana UP gives Rs 5 lakh interest-free loan + 10% subsidy to youth 21-40 years. Apply at msme.up.gov.in. Manufacturing, service, trade sectors.

hero.one_liner: CM Yuva Udyami Yojana UP (CM-YUVA) gives youth 21-40 a Rs 5 lakh interest-free, collateral-free loan plus 10 percent subsidy. Apply at msme.up.gov.in.

what_is_it: The Mukhyamantri Yuva Udyami Vikas Abhiyan Yojana, commonly known as CM Yuva Udyami Yojana or CM-YUVA, is a flagship entrepreneurship support scheme launched by the Uttar Pradesh government to encourage young residents of the state to start their own businesses. The scheme provides a structured combination of financial support and business facilitation to first-time entrepreneurs.

The scheme was introduced by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath as part of UP's push to reduce unemployment among educated youth and channel their energy into self-employment and enterprise creation. It targets the age group of 21 to 40 years, covering a wide range of young adults who are at the prime age for starting a business but often lack access to capital.

eligibility.label: Education and training
eligibility.value: At least Class 8 pass, plus a skill or training certificate (ODOP, Vishwakarma Shram Samman, UPSDM, ITI, or a relevant diploma or degree).

eligibility.label: Loan and subsidy
eligibility.value: Rs 5 lakh interest-free, collateral-free loan, plus a 10 percent margin money subsidy (max Rs 50,000).

eligibility.label: Clean record
eligibility.value: Not a defaulter with any bank, and not a beneficiary of another self-employment scheme.

eligibility.label: Sectors
eligibility.value: New business in manufacturing, service, or trade. One member per family.

how_to_apply.title: Visit the official MSME portal
how_to_apply.description: Go to msme.up.gov.in and look for the CM Yuva Udyami Vikas Abhiyan or CM-YUVA section. The portal also has a dedicated interface at msme1connect.up.gov.in. Avoid unofficial websites that may mimic the scheme portal.

how_to_apply.title: Register and create an applicant account
how_to_apply.description: Register on the portal using your Aadhaar-linked mobile number. OTP verification is required. After registration, log in and select the CM Yuva Udyami Yojana application form. Keep your Aadhaar, PAN, and bank account details ready before starting the form.

how_to_apply.title: Fill in the application form and business details
how_to_apply.description: Enter your personal details, address, educational qualification, age, and proposed business information. Select the eligible sector — manufacturing, service, or trade — and provide a brief description of the business you plan to start. Upload the required documents: Aadhaar, PAN, domicile certificate, age proof, caste certificate if applicable, and the project report.

how_to_apply.title: Submit and receive acknowledgment
how_to_apply.description: Review all entries before final submission. After submission, the portal generates an application reference number. Save this number for tracking. The application is reviewed by the district MSME office after submission.

how_to_apply.title: District MSME office verification
how_to_apply.description: The district MSME office reviews the application and may call the applicant for an in-person verification of original documents. The business plan is assessed for feasibility. After approval at the district level, the application is sent to the empanelled bank for loan processing.

how_to_apply.title: Bank loan sanction and disbursement
how_to_apply.description: The linked bank branch conducts its own KYC verification and sanction process. After sanction, the Rs 5 lakh loan is disbursed to your business bank account. The Rs 50,000 margin money subsidy is also credited to the loan account, reducing your repayment principal to Rs 4.5 lakh.

ministry: MSME and Export Promotion Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh

extra_sections.heading: What Is CM Yuva Udyami Yojana
content: Under CM Yuva Udyami Yojana, eligible applicants receive a business loan of Rs 5 lakh. This loan is interest-free and collateral-free, meaning the applicant does not pay any interest on the loan amount and does not need to pledge any property or asset as security for the loan.

In addition to the Rs 5 lakh loan, the government provides a margin money subsidy of 10% of the loan amount, which equals Rs 50,000. This subsidy does not need to be repaid; it is a direct grant from the state government to reduce the effective capital burden on the entrepreneur at the time of starting the business.

The loan is disbursed through participating banks and financial institutions empanelled under the scheme. The process is coordinated by the Uttar Pradesh MSME department, which facilitates the loan linkage between the applicant and the lending bank after application approval.

Businesses can be set up in any of three sectors covered under the scheme: manufacturing, service, and trade. Manufacturing covers production-based units such as small factories, food processing units, and handicraft workshops.

The CM Yuva Udyami Yojana represents UP's commitment to turning the state's large youth population into a productive economic force. With 21 crore people and a young demographic, UP stands to benefit significantly if even a fraction of its youth transition from job-seekers to job-creators through schemes like this.

extra_sections.heading: More Details and Coverage
content: The UP MSME department runs helpdesks at district MSME offices and through the MSME portal to assist applicants who face technical difficulties during the online application process. Applicants can also call the MSME helpline for guidance on documentation and eligibility queries.
Applicants should verify that their proposed business is genuinely new or at micro-enterprise scale. The scheme is not intended for established businesses seeking large-scale expansion capital.
The district MSME office reviews the business plan to confirm the enterprise falls within scope. Plans for very large-scale operations are redirected to other MSME credit channels.

extra_sections.title: You Need Training, Not Just a Business Plan
extra_sections.content:
A point many applicants miss: along with Class 8 pass, you must hold a skill or training certificate. This can be from ODOP, Vishwakarma Shram Samman, the UP Skill Development Mission, an ITI, or a relevant diploma or degree.

Without this training or qualification proof, the application is not eligible, even with a strong business plan.

extra_sections.heading: Who Is Eligible
content: Service covers businesses like repair shops, salons, coaching centres, and similar providers. Trade covers retail and wholesale businesses dealing in consumer goods.
The scheme covers both urban and rural applicants across all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh. There is no restriction based on district or region.
An applicant from a rural tehsil has the same eligibility as someone from a district town or city. Rural applicants are explicitly encouraged to apply through the gram panchayat-level CSC network.
A key feature of the CM Yuva Udyami Yojana is the path to extended credit. Applicants who repay the initial Rs 5 lakh loan within four years become eligible for an extended loan of Rs 10 lakh.

After receiving the loan and starting the business, applicants are encouraged to register on the Udyam Registration portal at udyamregistration.gov.in. Udyam Registration gives the business official MSME status, which opens access to government tenders, subsidies, and export promotion schemes.

extra_sections.heading: CM Yuva Udyami Yojana UP: Key Facts
rows: Mukhyamantri Yuva Udyami Vikas Abhiyan Yojana (CM-YUVA)
Rs 4.5 lakh after Rs 50,000 subsidy deduction
Rs 10 lakh — 50% interest-free after repaying first loan within 4 years
Aadhaar, PAN, domicile cert, age proof, bank details, project report

extra_sections.heading: The Loan and 10 Percent Subsidy
content: Of this second loan, 50% (Rs 5 lakh) is interest-free and the remaining 50% carries normal interest rates. This two-stage structure rewards disciplined repayment with access to larger capital.

This graduated loan structure is designed to reward repayment discipline and encourage sustainable business growth. Entrepreneurs who demonstrate the ability to run a viable business and repay the first loan are given access to larger capital to scale up.

The scheme is linked to the state government's MSME portal infrastructure. Applications are submitted online, and the entire process from application to loan disbursement is tracked digitally through the portal.
Eligible applicants must be permanent residents of Uttar Pradesh. Age must fall between 21 and 40 years at the time of application.

Women applicants between 21 and 40 years are fully eligible for the CM Yuva Udyami Yojana on the same terms as male applicants. The scheme does not differentiate based on gender, and women entrepreneurs in service or trade sectors are among the most common beneficiaries.

extra_sections.heading: How the Subsidy Actually Works
content: The applicant must not be a defaulter with any government scheme, bank, or financial institution. A clean credit history strengthens the application during the bank's KYC review.

The scheme covers applicants from all categories including General, OBC, SC, ST, and Minority communities. Reserved category applicants may be eligible for additional relaxations in eligibility criteria or processing, as announced by the state government from time to time.

Applicants are expected to submit a basic business plan or project report along with the application. This does not need to be a detailed financial model; a brief description of the proposed business, target customers, and estimated revenue is typically sufficient for initial screening.
Bank branches across UP are part of the lending network for this scheme. After approval by the MSME department, the application file is transferred to the linked bank branch for loan sanction.

Artisans and karigars with traditional craft skills — whether in weaving, pottery, metalwork, or wood carving — are well-suited candidates for this scheme. With the Rs 5 lakh loan, they can formalise their work, purchase better equipment, and scale output.

extra_sections.title: The Subsidy Is Back-Ended
extra_sections.content:
The 10 percent margin money subsidy, up to Rs 50,000, is not paid upfront. It is back-ended and credited after you repay the loan in full within four years without default.

The loan also has a four-year tenure that includes a short moratorium before EMIs begin. This is a Phase 1 benefit.

extra_sections.heading: The Two-Phase Loan Structure
content: The bank conducts its own KYC and verification before releasing the funds. This dual-review process ensures both government and bank oversight of every loan disbursed under the scheme.

Applicants under CM Yuva Udyami Yojana can set up a new business or expand an existing micro business, provided it falls within the eligible sectors. The scheme is not available for businesses that are already running at a scale larger than micro-enterprise as defined by the MSME Act.

The scheme complements other UP MSME support programmes such as the One District One Product (ODOP) scheme, which promotes district-specific products and gives visibility to locally produced goods. Entrepreneurs who set up businesses aligned with their district's ODOP product can benefit from both schemes simultaneously.
UP's MSME sector is one of the largest in India. The state has a strong base of traditional cottage industries, handicrafts, and small-scale manufacturers.

The CM Yuva Udyami scheme is distinct from the PM Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP), which is a central government scheme. PMEGP has higher maximum loan limits but goes through different application channels.

extra_sections.title: The Phase 2 Extended Loan
extra_sections.desc:
Repay the first Rs 5 lakh on time and you qualify for a second loan with a project cost up to Rs 10 lakh.

Phase 2 carries a 50 percent interest subsidy, and the government covers the CGTMSE guarantee fee. The structure rewards repayment discipline.

extra_sections.heading: How to Apply Online
content: CM Yuva Udyami Yojana is designed to bring the next generation of entrepreneurs into this ecosystem with formal financial support. It creates a clear pipeline from skill-trained youth to registered micro-enterprise owners.
The 10% margin money subsidy is funded entirely by the UP state government budget. It is not a loan; it is a non-refundable grant that reduces the repayment burden.

This feature distinguishes CM Yuva Udyami from typical bank loan schemes that carry no government subsidy. The grant is credited directly to the loan account after disbursement, reducing the principal immediately.

The CM Yuva Udyami Yojana portal at msme.up.gov.in provides information on eligible sectors, the application form, a list of empanelled banks, and FAQs. Applicants should check the official portal for the most current guidelines, as the state government may update the scheme terms or expand eligibility from time to time.
UP residents who meet the eligibility criteria for both may potentially avail each scheme for different business units. The two schemes are complementary and not mutually exclusive.

extra_sections.heading: Documents and Sectors Covered
content: Training and mentorship support is also provided to selected applicants under the scheme framework. The UP MSME department and associated agencies conduct orientation workshops to help new entrepreneurs understand basic business management, GST registration, and banking processes.

GST registration may be required for certain business types under the scheme. Applicants whose businesses are expected to cross the GST threshold should register on the GST portal in parallel with setting up the business.

The scheme encourages applicants to register their business entity — whether as a sole proprietorship, partnership, or private limited company — as part of the enterprise formalisation push. A registered business entity makes it easier to access future credit, open business bank accounts, and comply with tax requirements.

Applicants who have completed Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) training or any UP Skill Development Mission course are encouraged to apply for CM Yuva Udyami Yojana to convert their skill certification into a business. The scheme explicitly targets skill-trained youth who want to start their own enterprise.

Scheme beneficiaries who sell products or services through e-commerce platforms like Flipkart, Amazon, or Meesho can significantly expand their customer base. The MSME department periodically facilitates e-commerce onboarding workshops for scheme beneficiaries in cooperation with state industry bodies.

extra_sections.heading: After the Loan and Repayment
content: The CM Yuva Udyami scheme is separate from the UP Start-Up Policy, which targets tech-based startups. CM-YUVA focuses on traditional micro-enterprise sectors such as tailoring, catering, electronics repair, mobile repair, beauty services, small retail, and manufacturing of everyday products.

Applicants who receive the loan should maintain a separate bank account for the business. Mixing personal and business finances can complicate the annual review required under the scheme and may affect eligibility for the extended Rs 10 lakh loan.

The scheme documentation required for application typically includes Aadhaar card, PAN card, domicile certificate, age proof, educational qualification certificate (if applicable), bank account details, and a brief project report. Reserved category applicants additionally need a caste certificate.

Bank managers at branches linked to the CM Yuva Udyami scheme are briefed by the MSME department on the scheme's terms. Applicants who face delays or confusion at the bank branch level can escalate to the district MSME office for facilitation.

After the business is operational, maintaining proper accounts and filing GST returns (if applicable) helps build a formal financial track record. This track record is reviewed by the bank during the assessment for the extended Rs 10 lakh loan.

extra_sections.text: A 27-year-old UP resident who wants to open a mobile repair shop can apply for Rs 5 lakh interest-free under CM Yuva Udyami Yojana, get Rs 50,000 back as subsidy, repay the remaining Rs 4.5 lakh over 4 years, and then qualify for a Rs 10 lakh loan to expand. No collateral is needed at any stage.

extra_sections.heading: How CM-YUVA Fits UP's MSME Push
content: The UP government has set annual targets for the number of beneficiaries under CM Yuva Udyami Yojana. The rollout is phased with district-wise allocations reviewed each financial year.

Applicants who apply early in the financial year have a better chance of falling within the annual target. After a district's annual target is exhausted, new applicants may be waitlisted for the next financial year.

Young entrepreneurs who successfully scale their business using the CM Yuva Udyami loan and become MSME-registered units become eligible for other central government MSME support programmes, including the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) and Udyam Assist Platform benefits.

Applicants who anticipate repayment difficulty should plan their business cash flows carefully before availing the loan. Defaulting on this loan may affect eligibility for the extended Rs 10 lakh loan and future government support programmes.

Young entrepreneurs who receive the CM Yuva Udyami loan and successfully establish their business contribute to job creation at the local level. A business employing even two or three additional people multiplies the social impact of the scheme beyond the direct beneficiary.

extra_sections.heading: What Else to Know
content: Successful CM Yuva Udyami beneficiaries who grow their businesses and cross the MSME turnover thresholds are expected to graduate out of the micro-enterprise category. Their growth story contributes to UP's MSME ecosystem and can be cited by the government as evidence of the scheme's effectiveness.

UP has strong manufacturing clusters in cities like Agra (footwear), Varanasi (silk), Moradabad (brassware), Lucknow (chikankari embroidery), and Kanpur (leather). Young entrepreneurs in these cities who use the CM Yuva Udyami loan to enter these established industries have built-in market networks and supplier ecosystems to draw from.

extra_sections.title: Practical Tips and Process
extra_sections.content:
The CM Yuva Udyami scheme also fits within the broader National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM) and Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana frameworks for UP. District-level NRLM facilitators sometimes guide rural applicants in preparing their project reports and navigating the application process.

Applicants from minority communities should check the Minority Welfare Department's website in addition to the MSME portal, as some minority-focused loan schemes in UP complement or co-exist with CM Yuva Udyami and may offer additional support to minority entrepreneurs. The scheme's collateral-free nature is made possible through the government's guarantee backing, which reduces the risk for participating banks.

This is similar to the CGTMSE (Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises) model at the national level.

faqs.question: What is CM Yuva Udyami Yojana UP?
faqs.answer: CM Yuva Udyami Yojana (Mukhyamantri Yuva Udyami Vikas Abhiyan) is a UP government scheme that gives Rs 5 lakh interest-free, collateral-free business loans plus a Rs 50,000 margin money subsidy (10%) to residents aged 21-40 for starting businesses in manufacturing, service, or trade sectors. Apply at msme.up.gov.in.

faqs.question: What is the loan amount under CM Yuva Udyami Yojana?
faqs.answer: The loan under CM Yuva Udyami Yojana is Rs 5 lakh, interest-free and collateral-free. Additionally, the government provides a 10% margin money subsidy of Rs 50,000 as a non-refundable grant, reducing the net repayment obligation to Rs 4.5 lakh. After repaying the first loan within 4 years, the applicant becomes eligible for an extended Rs 10 lakh loan.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for CM Yuva Udyami Yojana UP?
faqs.answer: Permanent residents of Uttar Pradesh aged 21 to 40 years who want to start a new business in manufacturing, service, or trade are eligible. The applicant must not be a defaulter with any bank or government scheme. All categories (General, OBC, SC, ST, Minority) are eligible.

faqs.question: How do I apply for CM Yuva Udyami Yojana?
faqs.answer: Visit msme.up.gov.in and register using your Aadhaar-linked mobile number. Fill in the CM Yuva Udyami Yojana application form with personal details, business plan, and upload documents including Aadhaar, PAN, domicile certificate, and age proof. After district MSME office approval, the linked bank disburses the loan.

faqs.question: What is the margin money subsidy in CM Yuva Udyami Yojana?
faqs.answer: The margin money subsidy is 10% of the loan amount, equal to Rs 50,000, provided as a non-refundable grant by the UP state government. It is credited to the loan account after disbursement, reducing the principal the entrepreneur needs to repay to Rs 4.5 lakh.

faqs.question: Is collateral required for CM Yuva Udyami Yojana?
faqs.answer: No. The CM Yuva Udyami Yojana loan is completely collateral-free. Applicants do not need to pledge any property, asset, or guarantor to avail the Rs 5 lakh interest-free loan. The government's backing through the scheme framework reduces the bank's risk.

faqs.question: What sectors are covered under CM Yuva Udyami Yojana?
faqs.answer: The three eligible sectors are manufacturing (production-based businesses), service (repair shops, salons, coaching centres, and similar services), and trade (retail or wholesale businesses). All three sectors are open to applicants across UP, both rural and urban.

faqs.question: What is the extended loan under CM Yuva Udyami Yojana?
faqs.answer: After repaying the initial Rs 5 lakh loan within 4 years, the beneficiary becomes eligible for an extended loan of Rs 10 lakh. Of this extended loan, 50% (Rs 5 lakh) is interest-free and the remaining 50% carries standard interest rates. This is designed to support business scale-up.

faqs.question: What documents are needed for CM Yuva Udyami Yojana?
faqs.answer: Required documents include Aadhaar card, PAN card, UP domicile certificate, age proof, bank account details (with IFSC), caste certificate (for reserved category applicants), and a brief project report describing the proposed business. Educational certificates may also be requested by the district office.

faqs.question: What is the official portal for CM Yuva Udyami Yojana?
faqs.answer: The official portal is msme.up.gov.in. The scheme is also accessible through msme1connect.up.gov.in and upicon.in/cmyuva. The MSME Department of Uttar Pradesh administers the scheme. Applicants should use only official portals to avoid fraud.
